title: theOS's release and deploy
note: In the inbox: split from aip-6fb1 (its round 2). What theOS releases and where, production's ruleset, and the deploy at aven.maia.city.

source.text: theOS should be the authority over the whole release pipeline, avenSANDBOX included.

questions.q: What does theOS release, and where?
options: theOS's apps as a site at aven.maia.city, in place of avenOS, once checkpoint 3 is green (recommended)
Somewhere new: tell me where
Nothing public yet: releases are versions on GitHub only

questions.q: aven.maia.city also carries the Aven Peer: its relay (/relay, /ping, /healthz), /aven.json, and your vault and passkey for maia.city. When theOS's apps replace avenOS there, what happens to the Aven Peer?
options: It stays as it is: theOS's release replaces only the pages; the relay, /aven.json and the peer are untouched (recommended)
It is taken down with avenOS
Something else: tell me
questions.answer: Keep the Aven Peer, its relay and the vault's passkey as they are for now, in parallel with theOS's apps; we come back to this later.

questions.q: Should avenOS stay reachable anywhere once theOS's apps replace it at aven.maia.city?
options: No: its releases stay on GitHub and the undo can bring it back (recommended)
Yes, under a path of aven.maia.city: tell me which
Yes, on another host name: tell me which

questions.q: d-367c says theOS releases its apps once its release is green. What counts as green?
options: theOS's check command (aip-31df's crawl and docs check) passes inside avenSANDBOX's image on the commit released (recommended)
That, plus your try at Gate B of this intent
Something else: tell me
questions.answer: Yes: theOS's check command passes inside avenSANDBOX's image on the commit released.

questions.q: production's ruleset (aven/DB2/SANDBOX.md, your part 5) requires the checks 'Only from main' and 'avenSANDBOX', which came from avenDB's parked workflow. Is that ruleset set today, and may theOS's release workflow report checks under its own names, which you then put into the ruleset in place of the old ones?
options: Yes: it is set as written; theOS reports its own checks and I change the ruleset at Gate B (recommended)
It is set; keep the old names, and theOS's workflow reports checks under them
It is not set yet: tell me
questions.answer: Yes, with a step-by-step guide for what I need to do.

questions.q: Who starts theOS's deploy, and from where?
options: By hand, as before, in the environment production, and only from production (you limit the environment's branches to production) (recommended)
Automatically after every green release from production
By hand as before, from any branch
questions.answer: production starts the deploy automatically, the moment a change is merged into production and its release is green.
questions.note: Answered first as d-7994 (by hand); d-06a8 supersedes it in part: the deploy starts by itself the moment a change lands in production and its release is green, only from production.

questions.q: The environment production holds a secret MAIA_CITY_GUARDIAN_SECRET, which no file in the repository uses, while PRODUCTION.md says MaiaCityGuardian's secret stays offline with its holder. What is it, and should it stay there once production deploys by itself?
options: Delete it: the guardian's secret belongs offline; I keep my copy (recommended, if it is the guardian's private key)
Keep it: tell me what it is for
Keep it, and limit the environment to the branch production
questions.answer: MaiaCityGuardian is legacy (avenDB's): leave it, we don't care about it here.

questions.q: Gate A for aip-59ad, after spec review round 1 (every finding fixed): are its claims (c1, c3, c4, c5), assumptions, two checkpoints, outcome and mockup what must be true?
options: Yes
Change: tell me what
Send it back

questions.q: production's three required checks can be faked by a pull request that adds a workflow reporting the same names, because GitHub matches a required check by its name and source only. Merging still takes write access, which only you and your sessions have. Accept that the checks guard against mistakes, or add a guard no pull request can fake?
options: Accept: the checks catch mistakes; write access is the guard (recommended)
Add an organization ruleset 'Require workflows to pass' pinned to theOS's workflow (needs the organization's settings, possibly a paid plan)
Also require approval for every outside contributor's workflow runs (Settings, Actions)

items.text: avendeploy.yml (parked in .github/workflows-avendb/) is run by hand in the GitHub environment production. It needs the secrets HETZNER_API_KEY, HETZNER_S3_ACCESS_KEY and HETZNER_S3_SECRET_KEY, HETZNER_DNS_TOKEN, DEPLOY_SSH_KEY and DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS, and the variable AVEN_PEER_GUARDIAN; it stops before touching the server when the guardian is missing.

One run does six things in order: the bucket city-maia-aven, DNS A and AAAA for aven.maia.city, UDP 7501 and 7842 on the firewall maia-city, the Aven Peer (the image ghcr.io/myavenceo/aven/peer by digest, its own compose project in /opt/aven), Caddy, and health checks (/ping, /healthz and / over HTTPS, a probe peer direct and through the relay, the peer's record in the bucket).

Caddy is v1's container maia-city-caddy on v1's Hetzner server maia-city (Nuremberg). The deploy replaces only the lines between '# >>> aven.maia.city' and '# <<< aven.maia.city' of /opt/maia-city/deploy/Caddyfile (aven/ops/deploy/Caddyfile holds the block), validates the candidate, keeps the old file as /opt/aven/Caddyfile.before-<run>, then reloads.

The block sends /relay, /ping, /healthz and /generate_204 to the Aven Peer's relay, serves /aven.json (the peer's key and the RP ID maia.city) from /srv/site/aven, and serves everything else from /srv/site/aven/current as a single-page app (try_files {path} /index.html), with HSTS and nosniff.

aven/DB2/deploy/server/caddy.sh unpacks the release's aven-os-web-<version>.tar.gz (checked against SHA256SUMS on the runner) into site/aven/releases/<version>, switches the link site/aven/current, and keeps the three newest builds.

The last deploy is run 20 (31 Oct 14:13Z, from production at 5f6768d, PR #1750), successful; by its inputs' defaults it served the newest releases, avenOS 26.10.31v6 and avenPEER 26.10.31v5. Runs 17 to 19 were started from main and also succeeded, so the environment production does not limit which branch deploys.
This session cannot reach aven.maia.city: the environment's network policy refuses it (403 from the proxy), so what it serves now was not observed, only read from the last run's record.

problem.baseline: No theOS release exists: no tag, no GitHub release, no deploy. aven.maia.city serves avenOS 26.10.31v6 and the Aven Peer (avenPEER 26.10.31v5), deployed 31 Oct 14:13Z by avenDB's avendeploy.yml.
whys: theOS's apps cannot be opened at aven.maia.city. Why? Nothing releases or deploys them: the only release and deploy are avenDB's, parked.

Why? avenDB's pipeline releases avenDB's packages from production, built from aven/DB2, and deploys the Aven Peer and avenOS together in one run; theOS has no release job, no deliverable and no deploy of its own.
Why? The pipeline was built for avenDB (29 to 31 Oct) before theOS became the standalone project that owns the release (d-9351, d-a347).

Root cause: the release pipeline and the site at aven.maia.city belong to a legacy project, and theOS has not yet defined what it releases, how it is tagged, what gates it, and how its deploy is undone.
truths: A deployed server keeps serving what it was last given until something deploys again.
GitHub runs only workflow files in .github/workflows/ of the branch an event happens on; a status check that no workflow reports leaves a pull request that requires it unmergeable.
Caddy serves files from a folder; switching a symbolic link changes what it serves at once, and switching it back restores what was served.
A browser's storage and its passkeys belong to an origin and an RP ID, not to the page served there: a new page on the same origin leaves them as they are, unless the new page clears them.
A registered service worker stays until it is unregistered or its script answers 404 on an update check; a script answered with another type (HTML) only fails the update, and the old worker stays.
A GitHub release's assets stay downloadable until someone deletes them; git tags and the repository are public here, and so are Actions logs.
An Aven Peer's key, once lost, can't be recovered, and production's bucket is never wiped (aven/DB2/PRODUCTION.md).
A job that names an environment gets that environment's secrets; with 'No restriction', a job from any branch can name it.
assumptions: theOS's release changes only what aven.maia.city serves at its pages: the Aven Peer, its relay paths, /aven.json, its key, its bucket, DNS, the firewall and the vault's passkey stay as they are, in parallel, until Samuel comes back to them (his answer, 1 Nov).

A release is the theOS/ tree of one commit on production, taken by git archive and unpacked into its own folder on the server, named by the commit; nothing else is built or kept. No tags or release notes for now (deferred).
Changes reach production from main only, through a pull request; theOS's apps reach main first through the goal pull request (aip-6fb1).

The deploy runs by itself after every push to production that changes theOS/ and whose checks are green (d-06a8), in the environment production; its server step is learned from avenDB's caddy.sh (the link switch), never called from aven/.
'Green' means theOS's check command (aip-31df) passes inside avenSANDBOX's image on the commit released (aip-6fb1's c3) (Samuel's answer, 1 Nov).
avenOS is not kept reachable anywhere: its releases stay on GitHub, and the undo can bring it back (Samuel's answer, 1 Nov).
theOS/ is published whole: it is already public in the repository, so serving it adds no exposure.

The server is reached as deploy@aven.maia.city over SSH with DEPLOY_SSH_KEY, trusting only DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS (pinned under an alias, as v1's prod-ssh did); no Hetzner API is needed, since DNS and the firewall stay as they are.
aip-59ad builds after aip-31df's checkpoint 1 and aip-6fb1's checkpoint 4, and its first release follows the goal pull request that brings theOS/ to main.

Terms: v1 is maiaCITY's earlier app, which runs on the Hetzner server maia-city with the Caddy container maia-city-caddy; that Caddy serves /opt/maia-city/site on the server as /srv/site, so site/aven/current means /opt/maia-city/site/aven/current. The goal pull request is the repository's one pull request per goal into main (the repository's CLAUDE.md).

avenSANDBOX stays a required check on production (d-c219): theOS's workflow reports it, as the proof that the box of the commit released is built and works. The box itself is built and published by aip-6fb1's image workflow, on every push that changes theOS/sandbox/box, whatever production does.

DEPLOY_SSH_KEY and DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS stay repository secrets (d-ca32). Accepted: a workflow pushed on any branch by someone with write access could read them; the environment's branch rule guards theOS's deploy job, not those secrets.

production's ruleset is final for aip-59ad (Samuel, 1 Nov 10:52Z): it requires 'Only from main', 'avenSANDBOX' and 'theOS', all three from GitHub Actions; theOS's workflow must report jobs with exactly these names.

production's checks guard against mistakes, not against someone with write access (rv-d660, round 2): a pull request can report a required check's name from a workflow it adds. Only people with write access can merge into production. A guard no pull request can fake (an organization ruleset 'Require workflows to pass') is Samuel's to choose; asked.

The deploy is off (theOS/release/deploy.on holds off) until Gate B, so theOS's workflow can reach production before the first real release: Gate B's commit sets it on, and that push is the first deploy.
problem.risk: Can be undone, as long as the release touches only the served folder: every build stays on the server beside avenOS 26.10.31v6, and the undo switches site/aven/current back (c3). The undo is tried before it counts. Anything that touches the Aven Peer's key, its bucket, the passkeys' RP ID or the browsers' storage can't be undone and stays out of this intent (d-9364).

reuse.use: Learned from: run by hand in the environment production; release archive checked by SHA256SUMS before the server is touched; health checks from outside by the server's address; nothing secret printed, the repository is public. Its bucket, DNS, firewall and peer steps are not needed to serve static pages.

Learned from: the build unpacked beside the last, one link switched, three builds kept for a quick way back; only the marked block of v1's Caddyfile replaced, validated before reload, the old file kept.
Learned from: the relay paths and /aven.json stay with the Aven Peer; the rest is the site's. avenOS's single-page fallback (try_files {path} /index.html) does not fit theOS's several HTML pages.
Learned from: production takes changes from main only ('Only from main'); one release per changed package, tagged by date with v2, v3; a release's notes list its commits since the last tag.
Learned from: production's ruleset (no deletion, no force push, pull request with merge commits, two required checks); its check names belong to the parked workflow.
Used: the box a release runs theOS's check in, the same image on the runner and in a session.
Learned from: avenOS's service worker on the same origin; navigations go to the network first, so the new site shows when online.

claims.promise: theOS's release workflow reports three checks on every pull request to production, the three production's ruleset requires, and 'avenSANDBOX' and 'theOS' again on every push to production: 'Only from main' fails when the head is not main of this repository; 'avenSANDBOX' fails unless the box this commit describes (theOS/sandbox/box, tag theos-<hash>, built by aip-6fb1's image workflow) is published for amd64 and arm64 and its tools answer inside it (on the runner's amd64; arm64's tools are proven by avenSANDBOX's image workflow, which smokes each platform by digest before it tags the box); 'theOS' runs theOS's check command (aip-31df) inside that box through theOS/sandbox/run.sh and fails when the check fails. The three checks catch mistakes, not someone with write access: GitHub runs a pull request's workflows from its own code, and a required check is matched by its name and its source, GitHub Actions, so a pull request that adds or edits a workflow can report any of the three names green. Merging into production takes write access, which only Samuel and his sessions have (rv-d660, round 2).
claims.fails: A pull request from another branch merges; a red check passes; a check name differs from the ruleset's, so production stays blocked; production gets a commit whose box was never built; the commit deployed is not the commit checked.
claims.check: Job names compared letter for letter with the ruleset's. A pull request from another branch shows 'Only from main' red; a commit whose box tag is not published shows 'avenSANDBOX' red; a commit with a planted failing page shows 'theOS' red, then green without it. Checkpoint 1 ends with a real merge from main into production, all three green.

claims.promise: On a push to production that changes theOS/ and whose 'avenSANDBOX' and 'theOS' jobs are green, the deploy unpacks that commit's theOS/ tree into its own folder under site/aven/releases/, named by the first 12 hex of the tree's git hash (theos-<12 hex>), beside every earlier build, then switches the link site/aven/current to it; it writes nothing else but its own copy of the archive and the scripts in ~deploy/theos-release/: no Caddyfile, nothing in /opt/aven, no container, no DNS or firewall. aven.maia.city then serves exactly that tree, while /ping, /healthz and /aven.json answer as before. A push that leaves theOS/ as it was deploys nothing, so an undo holds until theOS/ changes. The deploy is off until Gate B: theOS/release/deploy.on holds off. production's pushes queue: a newer push replaces a waiting one, and the newest commit, which holds every earlier change, is the one checked and deployed.
claims.fails: The deploy touches the Aven Peer or Caddy's config (d-9364), serves a half-unpacked tree, or serves the dashboard in place of a missing file (Caddy's fallback) and still reports green.
claims.check: The server script runs against a temporary folder laid out like the server: a listing before and after shows changes only under releases/ and the links, the same tree changes nothing, a broken archive or one without index.html leaves current where it was. After each real deploy the health step fetches /, /docs/index.html, /avenCEO/index.html, /brain/index.html, /brain/ids.json and /aip/aip-59ad.json and compares each body byte for byte with the same file in the commit's tree (six files, not the whole tree); /ping, /healthz and /generate_204 must answer 200 or 204 and as before, /aven.json with the same body.

claims.promise: A theOS deploy is undone by one command: Actions, 'theOS undo', Run workflow, from production (.github/workflows/theos-undo.yml, in the environment production), which runs theOS/release/undo.sh on the server and switches site/aven/current back to the build before (site/aven/previous), or to the build named: 26.10.31v6 is avenOS, theos-<12 hex> a theOS build. Then aven.maia.city serves that build until a push to production changes theOS/. A deploy whose health step is red switches back to the build before by itself, and the job stays red.
claims.fails: The undo is untested, the earlier build is gone, or the undo leaves a mix.
claims.check: Tried in the temporary folder: theOS to theOS, undo again forward, back to avenOS after the first deploy and by name after two, a missing name refused; then once on the server at Gate B with Samuel: deploy, undo to avenOS, deploy again, the health step green each time.

claims.promise: The deploy job runs only for a push to production: it runs in the environment production (branch production only, d-f6da), needs that push's green 'avenSANDBOX' and 'theOS' jobs, and uses only the repository secrets DEPLOY_SSH_KEY and DEPLOY_KNOWN_HOSTS, which stay where they are (Samuel, 1 Nov); the key is written to a file with mode 600 and never printed.
claims.fails: theOS's deploy runs from another branch or for a red commit, or reads a secret it does not need (MAIA_CITY_GUARDIAN_SECRET, d-eb51; the Hetzner keys).
claims.check: At Gate A and again at checkpoint 2's review: the workflow's trigger, needs and environment read, and a grep of every secrets.* it names compared with the two expected.

outcome.promise: Over the first five theOS releases, or the first 30 days after the first one, whichever comes first, every merge into production that changes theOS/ is live at aven.maia.city within 15 minutes with no one starting anything by hand, and none needs an undo (the link switched back because the site served something wrong); Samuel opens aven.maia.city on his phone and his Mac and sees theOS's dashboard.
outcome.how: Read off the workflow's runs (merge time to the health step's green) and the record's events; Samuel's look at Gate B.

checkpoints.adds: theOS's release workflow (.github/workflows/theos.yml) with the jobs 'Only from main', 'avenSANDBOX' (this commit's box published and working) and 'theOS' (theOS's check through run.sh). After aip-31df's checkpoint 1 (the check command), aip-6fb1's checkpoint 4 (the check in the image) and the goal pull request that brings theOS/ to main. Ends with a real merge from main into production: production can merge again.

The deploy: theOS/release/deploy.sh (on the server: unpack beside every earlier build into theos-<tree hash>, keep the old target as previous, switch the link; the same tree changes nothing) and theOS/release/undo.sh, both tested in a temporary folder; theOS/release/ssh.sh (its own SSH setup, no legacy action) and health.sh (bytes compared, the Aven Peer's paths as before), tested against a local server; the deploy job in theos.yml, read by test.sh (c5). Gate B: the first real release, the undo to avenOS and back. The deploy ships off (deploy.on) with the undo workflow (theos-undo.yml); Gate B switches it on.
